newsitem.title: USA: Dole amassed considerable fortune during career.
newsitem.headline: Dole amassed considerable fortune during career.

text.p: Defeated Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole, who is bailing out embattled House Speaker Newt Gingrich with a loan, was wealthy before he lost last year's presidential race and could become even wealthier in retirement.

Gingrich announced on Thursday that Dole had given him a loan of $300,000 to pay off an ethics penalty imposed by the House of Representatives. Dole, who was defeated in last November's election by President Bill Clinton, said he was happy to come to the aid of a friend.

"I consider this not only an opportunity to help a friend but a long-term investment in the party," he said. "Today we bring this story to a close and a united Republican Party moves forward with its positive vision for the next millennum."

Dole and his wife Elizabeth released their tax returns for the past 30 years during last year's presidential campaign. They reported a joint income in 1995 of $583,869 and paid federal income tax of $171,665.

A financial report released last year by the Senate said the Doles were worth at least $2.3 million and possibly as much as $7.7 million. Their fortune was in widely diversified stocks and real estate as well as life insurance policies.

Dole's assets were between $500,000 and $1 million while the rest was in his wife's name. Elizabeth Dole this year returned to her post as president of the American Red Cross, from which she took a one-year leave of absence during the campaign.

Dole himself joined the law firm of Verner, Liipfert, Bernhard, McPherson and Hand, which lists tobacco companies among its clients. He has appeared in television commercials for Visa credit cards and stands to earn large amounts if he takes to the speaking circuit or writes his memoirs.

The loan to Gingrich is to be due and payable within eight years, collectible only from Gingrich, and cannot be forgiven, Gingrich's office said. It meets commercial bank standards for a loan of this amount and term and carries an interest rate of the prime rate plus 1.5 percent -- currently 10 percent.
